explanation: For a BUSINESS meeting, punctuality is expected and genuinely valued in Spain — guides consistently advise arriving on time or a few minutes early, even though Spanish colleagues themselves sometimes run five or ten minutes behind. Arriving deliberately late sends the wrong message about professionalism. The real flexibility in Spanish time culture shows up socially: dinners, parties, and casual get-togethers routinely start later than planned, and nobody minds.
local_tip: Arrive on time (or a few minutes early) for a business meeting, but don't be surprised or offended if your Spanish counterpart shows up a little late — that flexibility doesn't extend to you as the visitor.

also_check.note: Punctuality is strictly observed; arriving even five minutes late to a meeting is seen as disrespectful.
Arriving late to any meeting is a serious breach of etiquette; arriving early is the norm.
Similar to Spain's social norms, a 10-15 minute delay is common and unremarkable, especially outside formal business settings.
